text:
Amelia: Quick FYI — after merging selector change (commit ab3f9e4) we see a consistent tail-latency regression on the kv-batcher small-sequence job. p50 steady, p95/p99 up ~18-22%. I attached nsys traces to the buildkite artifact.
Raj: Which scenario exactly? small seq (128) or the long runs?
Sara: Small seq (seq=128) synthetic harness. Reproduced on canary and in CI. I ran nsys + nvprof to compare before/after kernel timelines. Summary below.
perf-bot: Auto-report: baseline mean token 13.4ms; post-change 16.5ms (+23%). Notable deltas: kernel_selector CPU time +3x, matmul_fused_v2 wall time +28%.
Amelia: Perfetto timeline (from our nsys->perfetto exporter) shows the selector thread spending much more time in a tight loop during packing, and device kernels are less overlapped across micro-batches. Looks like the batching window contracts.
Raj: Can you paste the exact profile command you used? I want to reproduce on my A40 rig.
Sara: I used:
``n
nsys profile --capture-range=nvtx --output=kv-after --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt --sample=all --force -- python run_batcher.py --scenario kv-small --seq 128 --batcher cfg/kv_batcher_small.json
```
Then exported csv + sqlite and converted to perfetto json with tools/convert_nsys_to_perfetto.py.
Tony: From quick nsys peek, CPU hotspot is kernel_selector_thread_loop. It's doing kernel_variant_probe for many micro-batches. Could be we probe multiple candidates per micro-batch synchronously.
Amelia: Exactly. The new selector probes preferred + fallbacks and returns a variant id that the batcher uses. We expected that to be amortized, but because variant isn't cached across the scheduling/packing cycle, each micro-batch re-probes. That multiplies cost proportional to number of micro-batches.
Sara: KV behavior hasn't changed in this commit. No eviction changes. The amplification is due to per-micro-batch probe calls during pack() time.
perf-bot: Kernel call diff (after - before): kernel_variant_probe +238%, matmul_fused_v2 +31%, copy_async -7%.
Raj: Proposed reproducer for bisect: revert selector probe loop + run ./run_perf.sh --scenario kv-batcher-small --iters 200 --collect nsight --seed 42 on an A100. Collect 3 nsys runs each for before/after. Upload to gs://redwood-perf/eng-runtime/bisect/2087654321/.
Ops-bot: @Raj assigned to thread (bisect-variant-probe). ETA 2h.
Raj: Starting revert now on my dev rig. Will push artifacts to gs when done.
(1h later)
Raj: Revert applied locally, ran 3 profiles. p99 returned to baseline on my rig. Uploading artifacts: sqlite, csv, perfetto json to gs://redwood-perf/eng-runtime/bisect/2087654321/runset.zip
perf-bot: Upload processed. Quick diff: kernel_variant_probe calls drop ~93%; matmul_fused_v2 total time down ~21%; p99 restored to baseline within noise.
Amelia: That points to probe loop being dominant. We should avoid probing per micro-batch. Proposal: add a per-scheduling-cycle variant cache keyed by (model_id, seq, quantization_tag) with TTL=cycle. Also emit a metric variant_lookup_count/request.
Tony: I'll prototype a small in-memory cycle-cache inside selector that caches variant for the duration of pack() and invalidates at cycle end. Will run the same harness.
Sara: Also add unit tests covering cache key collisions and TTL expiry semantics. We should have an e2e nsys job in CI so future selector work doesn't regress easily.
Tony: Prototype applied on dev, re-ran harness — p95/p99 back to baseline, perfetto timeline shows selector CPU time reduced and better kernel overlap.
Amelia: Great. Please open a PR with the selector-cache + metric and include the nsys before/after artifacts in the PR description (perfetto links). Tag @Sara @Raj for review. Also add an alert rule on variant_lookup_count/request > 0.5 for kv-batcher-small.
Perf-bot: Note: adding metric requires updating tracers repo (tracer-events) and dashboard panels. Filing tracker ticket.
Raj: After PR merges, plan a 24h soak on dedicated cluster to be safe; schedule under low-traffic window. Ops: can you run soak after merge?
Ops-bot: Will schedule a 24h soak on dedicated post-merge and collect perf traces at 1h intervals. Reminder: include perfetto JSON + sqlite in the soak artifact upload.
Sara: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4550 — "selector: cache variant per scheduling cycle; metric variant_lookup_count". Added unit tests and CI nsys job.
Tony: Left a note about TTL semantics in code comment and added a perf-test flag to force no-cache for debugging.
Amelia: Once CI nsys runs look good and soak passes, we'll cut a patch release. Thanks all.
Last message: perf-bot scheduled regression detector to run against next release window and will block if variant_lookup_count spikes.
